questions.q: Asexual reproduction takes place through budding in:
Which of the following is NOT a part of the female reproductive system in human beings?
questions.answer: (b) Vas deferens (part of the male system)

questions.q: Which part of a flower develops into the fruit?

The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma is called:
What is the importance of DNA copying in reproduction?
questions.answer: DNA carries the information for the body design. Copying DNA passes this information from parent to offspring, so the offspring are similar to the parent. Small errors in copying lead to variations, which help in survival over time.

questions.q: Give two advantages of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction.
questions.answer: (1) It combines DNA from two parents, so it creates more variation. (2) Variation increases the chance that some individuals survive if the environment changes, which helps the species survive.

In self-pollination, pollen is transferred to the stigma of the same flower (or another flower on the same plant). In cross-pollination, pollen is transferred to the stigma of a flower on another plant of the same species, by agents like wind, water or animals.

questions.q: Answer the following about events after fertilisation in a flower:

subparts.answer: It divides several times to form an embryo inside the ovule.

subparts.q: What do the ovule and the ovary develop into?
subparts.answer: The ovule develops into a seed, and the ovary develops into a fruit.

subparts.q: What happens to the petals, sepals and stamens?
subparts.answer: They may shrivel and fall off.

subparts.q: Name the hormones responsible for the changes at puberty in boys and in girls.
Give two changes seen in both boys and girls at puberty.
subparts.answer: (Any two) Thick hair grows in the armpits and genital area; the skin becomes oily and pimples may appear; height and weight increase quickly.

sections.note: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: A gardener wanted many rose plants with exactly the same flower colour as one prized plant. He cut small pieces of its stem with buds and planted them in moist soil. In another bed, he grew potato plants from pieces of potato that had 'eyes'. He also noticed that a Bryophyllum leaf lying on wet soil produced tiny new plants from the notches along its edge.

subparts.q: Name the method used to grow the rose plants.
What are the 'eyes' of a potato?
subparts.answer: Buds on the potato tuber (a modified underground stem).

subparts.q: Why do the new rose plants have the same flower colour as the parent? Give one limitation of this method.
subparts.answer: They are produced asexually, so they are genetically almost identical to the parent. Limitation: there is little variation, so all the plants may be equally affected by a disease or a change in the environment.
